title.narrative: Mainstreaming Nature-based Solutions in land-use systems for productive and resilient ecosystems

description.narrative: Mainstreaming nature-based solutions (NbS) in land-use systems for productive and resilient ecosystems
Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

Socioeconomic benefits to be delivered by the project at the national and local levels Strengthened capacities and enhanced cross sectoral coordination will promote integrated and sustainable management of ecosystems and their services in the Republic of Mauritius, with specific implementation of selected interventions in areas covering the project sites. The project will reduce ecosystem degradation and facilitate nature positive development by applying Nature-Based Solutions. The project will place nature at the center of human well-being and generate multiple environmental and societal benefits, through the following four components: Component 1 - Enabling policy environment for the governance and management of healthy and productive ecosystems. The Republic of Mauritius with limited land resources, has a high dependence on ecosystem services. These services are critical for livelihood, social well-being, and economic prosperity, encompassing water security, food production, disaster risk reduction (flood and erosion control), microclimate regulation, and recreational opportunities. While studies on ecosystem valuation exist, Mauritius lacks a formally endorsed national protocol. Consequently, current valuation methods primarily focus on direct economic benefits, such as timber prices for State Forest land. A more holistic approach that incorporates both direct economic values (e.g., wood and non-timber forest products) and indirect benefits (ecosystem services) is essential for Mauritius and Rodrigues, given their limited land resources. Assigning a monetary value to the various benefits ecosystems provide (such as clean water, flood control, fisheries) allows them to be directly compared with economic activities. This facilitates informed choices when considering development projects or resource allocation. It will encourage policies that promote conservation and sustainable land management practices, ensuring these ecosystem services continue to provide benefits for future generations. Valuation will also help to quantify the cost savings these ecosystems provide in terms of disaster risk reduction. By implementing ecosystem valuation, Mauritius can progress towards a more sustainable future where the value of its natural resources is recognized and factored into decision-making. The ecosystem valuation will therefore benefit the economy, environment, and well-being of its citizens. The development and adoption of a regulatory framework to support establishment of a carbon trading system will enhance the economic values attached to forest and tree protection. The framework will also ensure the fair and equitable trade of carbon trading and additional revenue to the country and communities engaging in tree cover enhancement. A multi-stakeholder platform to conduct an inter-sectoral policy review with key recommendations for integrated policy coherence will promote inclusive governance approaches and ensure national coordination in the country leading to consistency in decision making and ensure long term vision achievement. The multi-stakeholder platform will promote a more inclusive and effective approach to policy development, leading to more sustainable land management practices across terrestrial and coastal ecosystems, as well as agricultural lands in Mauritius. Land management issues in Mauritius touch on various sectors like agriculture, forestry, tourism, and infrastructure development. A multi-stakeholder platform will bring together representatives from these diverse groups, ensuring a holistic review that considers all aspects impacting land use. The different stakeholders have valuable knowledge and experience from their respective livelihood interests and lived experiences. The platform will foster communication and collaboration, allowing the stakeholders to share information and develop solutions that address the needs of all sectors. This can lead to more effective and integrated policies for sustainable land management and nature-based solution. The platform can also contribute to identify knowledge and data gaps, and promote social cohesion, as parties highlight their areas of contribution to support capacity gaps. When stakeholders are involved in the review process, they are more likely to understand the importance of the BGI project, understand NbS as a way to attain sustainable development, and feel invested in the success of the resulting policies. This broad ownership can lead to better implementation and enforcement. Necessarily, there will be competing interests regarding land use. The platform can provide a space for open dialogue and negotiation, allowing stakeholders to find common ground and develop workable solutions for sustainable land management and NBS. In addition, the platform can be used to engage the public in the policy review process. This transparency builds trust and fosters a sense of shared responsibility for sustainable land management in Mauritius. Component 2 - Nature-based solutions (NbS) for sustainable, resilient, and productive landscapes. Agroecology and agroforestry offer a promising approach for Mauritian farmers to improve their livelihoods, achieve greater economic security, and become stewards of a healthy environment. The adoption of agroecological principles and agroforestry at farm level to enhance production, soil fertility, and build resilience to climate change will reduce the dependence on chemical fertilizers and the economic cost related to it. Also, the externalities that the import of agricultural inputs represents will reduce considerable to provide a sustainable form of agriculture more beneficial in the short, medium, and long term. Moreover, agroecology practices such as cover cropping and compost application, improve soil fertility and water retention, leading to potentially higher yields and better drought tolerance. Increased plant diversity in agroecological systems generally attracts more beneficial insects like pollinators and natural predators, reducing pest problems and potentially improving crop yields. Agroforestry integrates trees with crops or livestock, providing additional source of income from fruits, timber and other non-timber products. This can also create opportunities for carbon sequestration projects or selling ecosystem services. By promoting healthy ecosystems and soil, agroecology and agroforestry can make farms more resilient to extreme weather events like floods and droughts, reducing potential losses. In addition to the direct economic benefits, agroforestry and agroecology offers several environmental benefits. Tree cover in agroforestry systems helps to reduce soil erosion from wind and rain. Agroforestry can improve water infiltration and retention in the soil, reducing need for irrigation and mitigating the impact of droughts. By creating diverse habitats, these practices promote biodiversity, which benefits the overall health of the ecosystem. Pesticide-free local bio-fertilizers, seed banks and domestic certification system to support transition to organic production and healthier living and eating, will be developed to sustain a healthy lifestyle with pesticide free and nutritious source of food leading to a healthier population and decrease in the cost of health expenses both at individual and national level. Agroecological practices can also help farmers access these premium markets, potentially fetching higher prices for their produce. NbS technologies will promote climate-resilient value chains through agroecological production methods to support the tourism sector and upscaled. This will give opportunities to better employment opportunities and promoting the destination as a nature friendly destination thus increasing the revenues from the sector as well. Locally sourced, environmentally-friendly food, can be a special appeal to tourists. Agroecology encourages a focus on local, seasonal food commodities. It can provide a reliable source of fresh, high-quality food for hotels and restaurants serving tourists and ultimately reduce reliance on imported food and strengthens the local economy. Agroecological practices can also be integrated with community-based tourism initiatives. Tourists can visit farms, learn about sustainable practices, and support local livelihoods, fostering a deeper connection with the destination. Agroecological practices promote healthier ecosystems and more scenic landscapes. This can align with the interests of tourists who may be interested in wildlife viewing or nature-based activities. Healthy ecosystems created through agroecology are more resilient to floods, droughts, and storms, which can disrupt tourism operations. Agroecology can contribute to protect tourism businesses and ensures a more reliable tourist experience. The afforestation of mangroves and climate resilient species carried out jointly with several stakeholders will further strengthen eco-tourist initiatives and at the same time promote a healthier environment that is resilient to the hazards of climate change. Mangroves act as natural barriers, protecting coastlines from erosion, storm surges, and floods. The mangroves reduce sedimentation and pollutants in lagoon, protecting coral reefs. Beside their protective function, restored mangroves and forests create stunning natural landscapes, providing scenic beauty for tourists who love nature. Healthy mangrove ecosystems also support diverse fauna, attracting wildlife enthusiasts and creating opportunities for activities like birdwatching, guided nature walks, and snorkeling near restored coral reefs protected by mangroves. Mangroves and coastal forests also provide opportunities for unique and educational ecotourism experiences. Tourists can learn about the vital role these ecosystems play in the environment, participate in projects like tree planting. This fosters a deeper appreciation for the natural world and a connection to the place. In Mauritius specifically, mangrove restoration efforts can be combined with existing attractions like boat tours in lagoons or kayaking adventures. Tourists can learn about the ecological importance of mangroves while enjoying the beauty of the restored habitat. Similarly, reforestation efforts in upland areas can be linked with hiking trails or birdwatching expeditions, allowing tourists to experience the restored forests while appreciating their role in preserving native wildlife and water resources. Ecotourism based on restored ecosystems can create economic opportunities for local communities living near these areas. They can act as guides, manage ecotourism lodges, or sell local crafts and products to tourists. Revenue generated from ecotourism can be channelled back into mangrove restoration and reforestation efforts, creating a positive feedback loop, where a healthy ecosystem attracts tourists, generating funds for further conservation and restoration. Component 3 - Unlocking private sector capital for improved ecosystem services and livelihood opportunities Public-private partnerships upscaling for restoration of high value ecosystems in threatened zones to support tourism and biodiversity will ensure that the barriers of limited resources are overcome and ensuring sustainability and inclusion of all the actors of society in protecting and preserving the fragile ecosystems. Examples of creation of new wilderness areas to increase tourist destinations to rehabilitated forests can be found at Ebony Forest in Chamarel and Ile aux Aigrettes Nature Reserve. The implementation of financial instruments in terms of incentives and insurance schemes once developed for private landowners and farmers to convert degraded lands to agroforestry will further enhance the quantity and quality of forests in the Republic of Mauritius which ultimately will provide a cleaner and healthier environment for the present and future generations. Incentives will also ensure the sustainability of the initiatives in the long term. These measures will also increase availability of locally produced fruits and vegetables that can further strengthen the supply to hotel chains and the local markets as well as food transformation. Component 4 - Knowledge management and learning for scaling. Peer partnerships among SIDS support centralized information platforms, biodiversity monitoring, community-based knowledge sharing, and best practices documentation will bring effective changes and additional knowledge base that can be deployed for the benefit of the communities. Raised awareness of farmers, government, and private sector in sector-specific strategies to protect critical ecosystems through farmer field school will further the continuity of the interventions post project and lay the foundations of a robust society based on best practices and sustainability. Benefits translate in supporting the achievement of global environment benefits The proposed outputs under component 1, on enabling policies for effective governance and management of healthy and productive ecosystems, will deliver environmental benefits from improvements in watershed and landscape rehabilitation and restoration, coastal zone management and protection and increase in vegetation cover and soil conservation. The outputs under component 2, on NbS for sustainable, resilient, and productive landscapes supporting food security will provide intrinsic adaptation benefits, which will increase resilience of livelihoods amongst vulnerable communities mainly the farmers and fishers through implementation of restoration and planting activities and agroforestry systems. As mentioned in the Core Indicators at Section B.2 about 17,000 ha of land area including degraded lands, water catchment and environmentally sensitive areas will be restored and reinstated through NbS to deliver improved functioning ecosystem services and improved production practices to improve watershed functions, reducing sedimentation and related costs to downstream water infrastructure; carbon sequestration; and higher productivity of land resources put under sustainable land management in Mauritius and Rodrigues, which will generate local and global environmental benefits and increase resilience to the deleterious impacts of climate change. Given the importance on environmental sustainability, the Government recognizes the natural resources as a key finite and fragile resource that plays an important role in supporting livelihoods, economic growth and ultimately human wellbeing as well as adapting to extreme weather conditions to the impacts of climate change. Adopting the NbS and integrated land management balances different stakes and needs of targeted stakeholders, while anticipating future impacts of economic development pathways and climate change; in order to meet multiple objectives such as land degradation neutrality, secure watershed services, biodiversity conservation, carbon storage, as well as to support resilient economic development, agricultural production and livelihoods. Promoting full and productive employment and decent work in rural areas Through the adoption of NbS, production of farming communities will be less vulnerable to climate change impacts and the also from extreme weather conditions. The direct effect on the farming community will be the production that goes according to their plans and thus securing their investments. The multiple products that would be produced throughout the year will ensure a constant income through out the year and therefore ensure a proper planning in the individual households therefore promoting constant employment opportunities and dignity. A value chain platform exists with the farmers community and hotel industry. To ensure higher standards of the hospitality sector, the project will support the promotion of bio/organic products in the tourism sector. There are growing eco-hotels, and facilities which require the sourcing of such produce from farmers and suppliers that offer organic options and/or are sustainably produced. The minimum wage threshold set up by the government would be implemented by beneficiary agricultural entrepreneurs towards their employees. This would also be complemented by accompanying measures by through incentives and subsidies to farmers and their employees who would enjoy constant income streams along with government support. Government commitments in line with the ILO declaration on fundamental principles and rights at work. The project will ensure fair and equal opportunities to everyone to access the project benefits and implement occupational health and safety standards in place as well as those of minimum wages and salaries as per the national laws guiding employment and its conditions associated with it including grievance mechanisms with a special focus on women groups, youth, disabled workers and wage labor. The project will also seek interventions that increase livelihoods thereby supporting greater financial stability for project participants.
